theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is an "external service" for a villa guest?
options: A service the villa staff do inside, such as cleaning
A bill the guest pays at the end of the stay for the room
A service from an outside business, such as a tour or a taxi
A repair to the outside of the villa, such as the roof

questions.stem: A guest asks you to "set up something fun for tomorrow". What should you do first?
options: Ask about their interests, budget, group size and timing
Book the most costly tour so that they get the very best
Give them a pile of leaflets and leave them to choose

options: On any roadside sign you saw on your way to work
On a social media post shared by a stranger
From a person who stops guests at the villa gate
In the villa's approved supplier list

BSJ

Whether the guide supports the same football team

options: Give them some tablets from your own bag
Call a doctor from the villa's approved doctor list

options: Call the guest's family overseas to ask what to do
Drive the guest to a clinic in your own car

questions.stem: In Jamaica, which number do you call for an ambulance or the fire service?
A guest asks where to buy the medicine the doctor has ordered. Where should you send them?
options: To a shop on the street that sells loose tablets
To another guest who may have the same medicine
To a bar, as they may have something for the pain

Only those who need to know, such as the doctor

That the babysitter is any friend of a staff member

options: Only the name of the tour company and its logo colours

options: So that any staff member can check or follow it up

options: Tell the guest to wait, as the taxi will come in time

options: Tell the guest that it is not the villa's problem
Arrange another licensed taxi and tell the guest

Drive them yourself in your own car without asking

questions.stem: Why do you ask guests how their tour went when they come back?
options: To check the service was good and improve future advice
To find out how much money they spent on the trip
To ask them to pay you a tip for the booking
To decide whether they can book another tour

options: Tell the guest that all the guides there behave like that

questions.stem: What is an "airport transfer"?
options: Changing from one flight to another at the airport
A booked ride between the airport and the villa

A refund for a cancelled flight ticket

questions.stem: Guests land at the airport in Montego Bay at 2:00 p.m. They need about 1 hour to clear the airport, then the drive takes about 1 hour 30 minutes. About when will they reach the villa?

options: Only whether the raft is painted a nice bright colour
That the tour starts after the child's bedtime
That children may go and life jackets fit

questions.stem: A guest uses a wheelchair and wants to visit an attraction. What should you check first?
options: Whether the attraction sells souvenirs
Whether it has ramps and access for wheelchairs

questions.stem: Which information about an attraction is most useful to give a guest?
options: Its history only, with the year it was first built
The names of all the staff who work there
Gossip you heard about the owner's family
Opening hours, price, location and what to bring along

questions.stem: A storm warning is given for tomorrow. A guest has a boat trip booked. What should you do?
options: Check with the operator and update the guest
Tell the guest to go anyway, as the boat is strong
Say nothing, as the weather is not your concern
Cancel the guest's whole holiday at the villa

questions.stem: What will a car rental company usually ask a guest to show?
options: Only a key card from the villa where they stay
A letter from the villa manager
A library card and a utility bill
A valid driver's licence and a credit card

questions.stem: A guest wants to hire snorkel gear from an outside shop. What should you check?
options: That it is the oldest gear in the shop, so it costs less
That the guest pays you in cash, and not the shop itself
That the shop is trusted and the gear is safe and clean
That the gear has not been cleaned since the last user

questions.stem: Why should you know the local area well?
options: To give guests correct directions and advice
To find the cheapest places for your own shopping
So that you never have to use the villa supplier list
To tell guests which areas you personally dislike

questions.stem: A guest pays a tour company through the villa. What must you give the guest?
options: A spoken thank you, as no paper is needed
A receipt showing the amount and the currency
A handwritten note with your name on it only
A copy of the villa's bank statement for the month

questions.stem: A guest wants a tour charged to their villa account. What should you get?
options: Nothing, because the guest's word is enough
The tour guide's signature on a blank page
Money from one of the guest's friends
The guest's signature on the charge slip

questions.stem: What should the external services log show for each booking?
options: The service, date, time, supplier, cost and who booked it
Only the guest's first name, written in pencil
The tip you hope to get from the guest for it
The guest's passport number and their age

questions.stem: A guest asks for a service that is not available in the area. What is the best reply?
options: Say no and walk away from the guest
Promise it anyway and hope to find one later

questions.stem: When is it best to book a popular tour for a guest?
options: On the morning of the tour, when you get to the gate
As early as possible, once the guest agrees
Only after the guest has gone back home

options: The weather forecast for the rest of next week
The name of the guest's travel agent

essays.stem: Describe how you would find out what a guest needs before you arrange an outside service for them.
essays.modelAnswer: I would greet the guest by name, smile and give them my full attention. I would ask open questions, such as "What do you enjoy doing on holiday?" and "What would you like to see in Jamaica?" I would find out how many people are going, including children or older guests, and the date and time that suits them. I would ask about their budget, whether they want a private or shared trip, and any special needs, such as a wheelchair, an allergy for a lunch stop or a fear of boats. I would listen carefully, make notes and repeat the main points back to check that I have understood. Then I would offer two or three suitable choices from the approved list, with honest information on each, and let the guest decide.
markingPoints: Greets politely and gives full attention
Asks open questions about interests and what they want
Finds out numbers, date and time, budget and private or shared
Asks about special needs (access, diet, health, children)
Notes and repeats back, then offers suitable choices for the guest to decide

essays.stem: Explain why the villa keeps an approved list of licensed suppliers, and say what should be checked before a supplier is added to it.
essays.modelAnswer: The villa keeps an approved list so that guests are sent only to businesses that are safe, honest and reliable. If a guest is hurt or cheated by an outside business, it harms the guest and the villa's name. An approved list also saves time, because staff do not have to search each time, and every staff member gives the same good advice. Before a supplier is added, the manager checks that it holds the right licence for tourism or transport in Jamaica, and that it has insurance. The vehicles, boats and equipment should be in good condition, with safety gear such as life jackets and seat belts. The manager also checks prices, what is included, cancellation rules, opening times and how to contact them, and asks for reviews or feedback from past guests. The list is checked again often and updated.
markingPoints: Protects guests' safety and the villa's name
Saves time and gives guests the same reliable advice
Check licence and insurance
Check vehicles, boats and safety equipment
Check prices, terms, contacts and feedback, and keep the list up to date

essays.stem: Describe the steps for booking an airport transfer for a guest, from taking the request to the day of travel.
essays.modelAnswer: First, I take the guest's details: name, number of people and bags, the date, the flight number and time, and which airport. For a departure, I work back from the flight time and allow enough time for the drive and the airport check-in, so I agree a pick-up time with the guest. Next, I call a licensed transport company from the villa's approved list, check that a suitable vehicle is free and agree the price and currency. I give only the details they need. I write the booking in the log book with the reference number, and give the guest a confirmation slip with the pick-up time, place, cost and the driver's company. The day before, I confirm with the company. On the day, I check that the driver arrives on time, help with the luggage and record that the transfer went ahead.
markingPoints: Takes the guest's full details (names, numbers, bags, date, flight, airport)
Works out and agrees a suitable pick-up time
Books a licensed operator from the approved list, agreeing price and currency
Records it in the log and gives the guest written confirmation
Reconfirms the day before and checks on the day

essays.stem: A guest asks for a doctor because they feel unwell, but it is not an emergency. Describe what you would do, and how you would protect the guest's privacy.
essays.modelAnswer: I would stay calm and kind, ask the guest how they feel and whether they want a doctor to visit the villa or prefer to go to a clinic. If at any time the guest seems seriously ill, I would call an ambulance at once. I would call a doctor from the villa's approved list, give the doctor the guest's name, where they are and a short note of the problem, and agree the visit time and fee. I would tell my supervisor. I would not give the guest any medicine of my own. When the doctor arrives, I would show them to the guest, then leave so that they can talk in private. Afterwards I would help with a pharmacy if needed. I would only tell the people who need to know, keep any notes locked away, and never talk about the guest's health with other guests or staff.
markingPoints: Calm, caring check of what the guest wants; ambulance if it becomes serious
Calls a doctor from the approved list with the right details and agrees time and fee
Informs the supervisor and does not give medicine
Lets the doctor and guest talk in private; helps with the pharmacy
Shares health information only with those who need to know and keeps notes secure

essays.stem: Compare a private tour with a shared group tour, and say which you might suggest for different kinds of guest.
essays.modelAnswer: A private tour is only for the guest's own party. The guide and the vehicle are theirs, so the times can be changed, the guide can stop where they like, and it feels personal and quiet. It costs more per person. A shared group tour mixes guests from different places on a set route and timetable. It costs less per person and can be fun and social, but there is less choice of times, the group may have to wait for others, and the bus may stop at several hotels on the way. I might suggest a private tour for a honeymoon couple, a family with small children who need breaks, a guest who uses a wheelchair, or a VIP who wants privacy. A shared tour may suit a single traveller who wants to meet people, or guests on a budget.
markingPoints: Private: own party, flexible times and stops, more personal
Private costs more per person
Shared: cheaper, social, but set times and stops for others
Suggests private for suitable guests (couple, family, access needs, VIP)
Suggests shared for suitable guests (single traveller, budget)

essays.stem: Describe the information and safety advice you should give a guest before they go on a tour or trip away from the villa.
essays.modelAnswer: I would give the guest the confirmation with the date, the pick-up time and place, the company's name and phone number, the cost and what is included, such as lunch or entry fees. I would tell them how long the trip lasts and what to bring, for example sunscreen, a hat, water, comfortable shoes, swimwear and a little cash in J$ or US$. I would advise them to use only the licensed guide and vehicle that was booked, to wear the life jacket or seat belt given, and to follow the guide's instructions. I would remind them to keep passports and valuables in the villa safe, to carry only what they need, and to buy only from licensed vendors. I would give them the villa's phone number in case of any problem, and ask them to call if they will be late.
markingPoints: Gives booking details: date, time, place, company contact, cost and inclusions
Says how long it lasts and what to bring (sun protection, water, shoes, cash)
Use only the booked licensed operator; wear life jackets or seat belts; follow the guide
Keep valuables safe; buy only from licensed vendors
Gives the villa's contact number for problems

essays.stem: Explain how you would deal with a problem with an outside service, such as a late taxi or a tour that is cancelled.
essays.modelAnswer: I would act quickly and stay calm. First, I would call the supplier to find out what has happened, using the booking number, and ask how soon they can fix it. If the taxi will be too late for the flight, I would book another licensed taxi from the approved list. If a tour is cancelled, for example because of bad weather, I would ask the company for another date or a refund, and look at other choices the guest may like. I would tell the guest honestly and politely what has happened, say sorry for the trouble, and give them the choices. I would tell my supervisor and write the problem, the steps taken and the result in the log book. Later, I would follow up with the guest, and the manager may review whether to keep using that supplier.
markingPoints: Acts quickly: calls the supplier with the booking number
Arranges a licensed replacement, new date or refund
Tells the guest honestly and politely, says sorry and offers choices
Informs the supervisor and records it in the log
Follows up with the guest and reviews the supplier

essays.stem: Explain how to handle costs and payments when you arrange an outside service for a guest, including payments in J$ and US$.
essays.modelAnswer: Before booking, I tell the guest the full price, the currency it is in and what it includes, and whether a deposit or cancellation fee applies, so there are no surprises. If the guest wants to pay in the other currency, I use only the exchange rate the villa sets for that day, and show the guest the sum. Any tax is added at the current rate shown by the supplier. If the guest pays the supplier directly, I tell them how. If the villa pays and charges the guest's account, I get the guest's signature on a charge slip and post it to their account. If I take cash, I count it in front of the guest, give a receipt with the amount and currency, and hand the money in with the paperwork. I never add my own extra charge, and I record every payment in the log.
markingPoints: Tells the guest the full price, currency, inclusions and any deposit or fees first
Uses only the villa's exchange rate for that day and shows the sum
Charges to the account only with the guest's signature on a slip
Counts cash, gives a receipt with amount and currency, hands it in
Honest: no extra charges; every payment recorded

essays.stem: Explain why villa staff must give honest advice about outside services, and how they should deal with touts or offers of money from suppliers.
essays.modelAnswer: Guests trust villa staff to tell them the truth, because they do not know the area. If staff send guests to a business only because they are paid to, the guest may get a poor or unsafe service, and they will blame the villa. Honest advice builds trust, good reviews and repeat guests, and it protects the good name of tourism in Jamaica. Staff should recommend services that suit the guest, explain the good and bad points and the real prices, and use the approved list. If a driver or tour seller offers a staff member money to send them guests, the staff member should politely refuse and report it to the supervisor. Touts who approach guests at the gate or on the beach should be dealt with calmly; staff should not argue, but should guide guests to licensed services and tell security or the supervisor.
markingPoints: Guests rely on staff, so advice must suit the guest, not the staff member's gain
Poor or unsafe services harm the guest and the villa's name
Honest advice builds trust, good reviews and repeat business
Refuse offers of money from suppliers and report them
Deal calmly with touts; guide guests to licensed services and inform security or the supervisor

essays.stem: Describe the records you would keep for outside services, and explain why following up with the guest afterwards matters.
essays.modelAnswer: For each request I would write in the external services log the date and time of the request, the guest's name, the service, the supplier, the date and time of the service, the number of people, the cost and currency, how it is paid, the booking number and my name. I would keep a copy of the confirmation slip and any receipts. Changes, cancellations and problems are also written down. These records let any staff member check a booking or answer the guest, help the office match payments and bills from suppliers, and show which suppliers are used most. Following up with the guest, by asking how the trip went, shows care and lets me put right anything that went wrong. Good and bad comments are recorded and passed to the supervisor, so that the villa can keep using good suppliers and stop using poor ones.
markingPoints: Log details: request date, guest, service, supplier, time, numbers, cost, payment, booking number, staff name
Keeps confirmations and receipts; records changes and problems
Records let anyone follow up and help match payments
Follow-up shows care and lets problems be put right
Feedback passed on to improve the choice of suppliers

practical1.title: Role play: arrange a tour and an airport transfer for villa guests
practical1.brief: Set up a guest services desk in the Centre's training room, with a phone (or a phone card for role play), the made-up approved supplier list the assessor gives, booking forms, confirmation slips and an external services log. The assessor gives each member a request card, for example: a family of four with a 5-year-old who want a river rafting trip; a couple who need an airport transfer to Montego Bay for a 4:15 p.m. flight; a guest who wants a table at a seafood restaurant; a guest who wants to rent a car; a guest who wants a snorkelling trip. Each member in turn plays the guest services agent: greets the "guest" (another member), finds out the needs, chooses a suitable licensed supplier from the list, "phones" the supplier (played by another member), agrees the details, price and currency, fills in the booking form, writes the confirmation slip, explains it to the guest and records it in the log. The assessor then gives one change or problem (for example, the time changes or the tour is full) for each member to handle. Photograph each stage below and add the photos, forms, slips and log pages to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A desk, chairs and a phone (or a role-play phone card)
A made-up approved supplier list with prices in J$ and US$, contacts and terms (from the assessor)
Request cards and change or problem cards (from the assessor)
Booking forms, confirmation slips and an external services log
A calculator, pens and a phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The guest services desk set up with the supplier list, forms and log
A member finding out a guest's needs
The "phone call" to the supplier, with the booking form being filled in
A completed booking form and confirmation slip for each member
The confirmation slip being explained to the guest
The external services log with every booking recorded
A change or problem being handled, with the updated record
checklist: Greeted the guest politely and found out the needs with open questions
Chose a suitable licensed supplier from the approved list
Gave the supplier only the details needed, and kept the guest's room number private
Agreed and recorded the date, time, place, number of people, price and currency correctly
Wrote a clear, correct confirmation slip and explained it to the guest
Recorded the booking in the log with the booking number and their name
Handled the change or problem calmly and updated the records
Took part in every role: agent, guest or supplier
safety: Use only made-up guest names and details
Recommend only licensed operators with safety equipment
Keep the area clear of trailing phone cables and bags
Keep forms with guest details secure at the end of the session

practical2.title: Make a guest services directory and handle requests for medical and other outside services
practical2.brief: Using the made-up information sheet the assessor gives (local transport, tours and attractions, doctors, a pharmacy, the nearest hospital, a dry cleaner, a babysitting service and restaurants), make a guest services directory for a villa as an A4 folder or poster. Each member writes one section, with the name, what is offered, opening hours, phone number, price range and any safety tips, in clear, friendly words. Add the emergency numbers and a short "what to do in an emergency" box. Then each member role plays one request with a "guest" (another member): for example, a guest who feels unwell and wants a doctor to visit, a guest who needs a pharmacy, parents who want a babysitter, a guest whose suit needs dry cleaning by tomorrow, or a guest whose taxi has broken down. Use the directory, make the arrangement, protect the guest's privacy, tell the "supervisor" (the assessor) where needed and record it in the log. Photograph each stage below and add the photos, the directory and the log to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A made-up information sheet of local services (from the assessor)
A4 or A3 card or a folder with plastic sleeves, rulers and coloured pens
An external services log, message pads and pens
A phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The group planning the sections of the directory
The emergency numbers and emergency box
A request being handled, using the directory
The log with every request recorded
checklist: Wrote a clear, correct, friendly section for the directory
Included hours, contacts, prices and a safety tip for their section
Used the directory to find a suitable service for the request
Kept health and personal details private and shared only what was needed
Did not offer any medicine and called for help correctly when the case was serious
Told the supervisor where needed and recorded the request in the log
Spoke to the guest politely and checked that they understood the arrangement
safety: In any real emergency, stop the role play and follow the Centre's emergency procedure
Never give medicines; refer to a doctor or pharmacist
Use only made-up guest names and health details
Keep scissors and craft knives (if used) closed and stored when not in use
